name: Avantor, Inc.
moat_justification: Real distribution scale and spec-in embedment, but economics say narrow: ROIC proxy ran 5.2–9.3% in FY19–FY24 (never durably above cost of capital), gross margin is eroding, revenue has fallen three straight years, and the Distribution unit itself was written down $785M in Q3 2025. That is a weak-moderate moat, not a wide one.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 9.0x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Levered lab-distribution turnaround, moat 4/10 — does not clear 15% on any scenario (weighted IRR 5.90%, IV@15% $4.50 vs $16.42 price); it would need to fall to ~$4.50 to clear the 15% hurdle on TTM owner's earnings.
moat_for: VWR distribution scale: one of the two largest global lab distributors, 300,000+ customer locations in ~180 countries
Spec-in stickiness: materials specified into 85% of the top 20 commercialized biologics — recurring bioprocessing demand
Proprietary brands with regulatory trust: J.T. Baker high-purity chemicals, NuSil medical-grade silicones
cGMP / regulated-workflow embedment raises switching friction in production (not just research) labs
moat_against: Distribution is contestable — larger platforms (Thermo Fisher et al.) compete for the same lab spend
Revenue down three straight years (FY23–FY25) and the Distribution unit took a $785M goodwill impairment in Q3 2025 on market conditions and projected performance
ROIC proxy only 5–9% across FY19–FY24 (negative in FY25 on the impairment) — at/barely above cost of capital
Gross margin eroding: 34.6% FY22 → 32.7% FY25 → 32.1% TTM
Levered: net debt $3,580,900,000 = 9.0x normalized OE on the TTM base
